Karan Virwani: 
Thank you, Michelle, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us for our Q2 and 
first half FY27 results. As always, the financials we discuss today are on an I-GAAP-equivalent 
basis. The reconciliation to reported Ind AS is in the presentation and our shareholder letter. 
Before we turn to the numbers, I want to start where everything we build starts. 
WeWork is the brand India's companies look for first when they choose where to work. We 
pioneered this category in India, we lead it today, and that brand is the foundation of everything 
that we do. Our vision is an ecosystem where people feel supported, energized, and inspired to 
do their best work. 
Our mission is to build spaces that don't just enable work; they elevate it. It shapes how we 
design WeWork spaces, how we operate it, and how our members experience it to the same 
standard day one in any city. The market around us has had another strong quarter. India 
absorbed 21 million square feet of office space in Q3, up 6% year-over-year, with GCCs taking 
about 41% of it. 
Flex took 24% of all leasing, about 5 million square feet, which is up 21%, ahead of BFSI at 
22% and tech at 15%. It has now been India's largest occupier segment for three quarters running. 
Two nuggets from the quarter that stand out for us: domestic companies took 47% of all leasing, 
and flex operators drove half of that. Hyderabad led the country with 25% of Q3 leasing, a 
market where we have doubled down this year. 
The move to quality also continued, with 80% of completions being green-certified, and about 
three quarters of leasing in buildings under 10 years old, the same segment our portfolio sits in. 
Flex has gone mainstream, and branded workspaces are the most relevant form. Of India's 
billion-plus square feet of office space, Flex is about 123 million, organized Flex about 83 
million, and organized branded workspace, a category we pioneered, about 29 million. 
We operate about 10 million square feet of WeWork-branded spaces, by our estimate about 26% 
of the space and 34% of the revenue. That premium reflects how deeply our members build

around us. Once a company is inside the ecosystem, WeWork becomes part of how it runs, not 
just where it sits. 
The demand comes from a change in how companies plan. Few can say how many people they 
will need or where a year from now, they're going to be, and five-plus year leases have collapsed 
from 40% of enterprises to just 8%. A new hire joins in 45 days to 60 days, while a team can be 
live in a WeWork space on day one, with no fit-out and no capex. 
And companies are trading up to keep their people, with 55% of those planning or moved to 
targeting better buildings. Loyalty in Flex is never locked in; it's earned at every renewal. 
Companies choose WeWork first because the brand defines the category. 96% of companies that 
are not yet members already know us, against a 51% median for other operators.  
We bring a global network of more than 600 locations in 37 countries, with 1 in every 4 Global 
Fortune 500 companies as a WeWork member worldwide. The backing of the Embassy Group 
and our relationship with India's leading developers put us in the right buildings, with about 94% 
of our portfolio in Grade A across 8 cities that take roughly 95% of the country's Grade A 
absorption. 
 
They stay because the network grows with them. Our NPS is +79. More than 16,000 accounts 
work with us, and of those using our physical spaces, nearly 30% work across more than one 
format, moving from a day pass to a managed office floor without ever leaving the network. And 
27% already buy from us beyond the desk. This is where the platform begins. 
 
This is a category we created and the one that we own. AI and macro uncertainty are reshaping 
how companies grow, and they are now committed -- they now commit to teams before they 
commit to buildings. Branded workspaces and WeWork-branded workspaces are the most 
relevant answer to that. 
WeWork is the most future-ready form, one standard in every city, life from day one, and able 
to grow and shrink or move with the business. That's the story of this quarter. Demand is keeping 
pace with our largest openings. Our platform is compounding beyond the desk, and margins, 
returns, and cash, all strengthening throughout the build. 
 
We added nearly 11,700 desks in Q2, more than we've ever opened in a quarter, taking us to 
145,300 desks across 85 centres in 8 cities, which is up 27% year-over-year, with about 18,400 
added in the first half and about 4,500 more added in October. We are past the 22,000 mark that 
we set out for in Q1. 
 
Members grew 32.5% to about 121,700, ahead of capacity, and occupancy grew 357 basis points 
year-over-year to about 83.7%, with mature centres at nearly 88%. The 114-basis points dip 
from Q1 is new capacity ramping up, and mature centres have edged up over the same period. 
 
Demand carried straight through to the numbers. Revenue grew nearly 31.6% year-over-year 
and 10.1% quarter-over-quarter to about INR768.7 crores. EBITDA grew faster, at about 37.6%

at 1.5 times EBITDA. In H1, FCFO more than doubled, up 157% to INR379.8 crores, which is 
already nearly two-thirds of the INR586 crores we generated in all of FY26. 
 
That cash is funding our growth in full. After INR175.8 crores of capex in the quarter, we still 
generated INR61.9 crores of free cash flow to the firm. In H1, that FCFO funded our entire 
INR363.8 crores of capex, the largest we have ever deployed, and left a surplus of INR16 crores. 
That surplus has strengthened the balance sheet. We closed September with a net cash of 
INR23.1 crores, compared with a net debt of INR310.5 crores a year ago. 
Our credit rating was upgraded from an A- to A+ over the year, and our average cost of 
borrowing fell 184 basis points to 8.5%. Our reported Ind AS basis PAT was INR20.5 crores,
